narrative.what_i_did: Migrated tapit-wallet to comms v2. Deleted the five old comms files (appcommander/comms/current.json + interactions.jsonl + in-flight.jsonl + carpenter-opinions.md, appcommander/foreman-context/carpenter-state-for-foreman.md) via git rm. Created .carpenter/ at the repo root with a .carpenter/archive/ subfolder (both tracked via .gitkeep). Wrote .carpenter/session.json as the single canonical comms file. Wrote .claude/hooks/session-close.sh (Stop/PreCompact hook that archives a timestamped copy, commits, and pushes main) and .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (SessionStart hook that pulls main and surfaces the prior session's narrative via jq). Both hooks chmod +x. Merged the new hook entries into the existing .claude/settings.json without overwriting the three pre-existing hook entries (SessionStart → scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs, UserPromptSubmit → grounding-gate echo, Stop → scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs); the new bash hooks coexist with the existing node scripts inside the same hooks arrays. Added a PreCompact block carrying only the new session-close.sh. This is the first session.json written; from here forward every session reads this file at start and overwrites it at end.
narrative.whats_pending: Three follow-up items that the migration did NOT touch and should be operator-decided next session. First, CLAUDE.md still extensively documents the retired five-file comms protocol and the closed-loop CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md hand-off; that doctrine block should be rewritten to describe the comms v2 .carpenter/session.json loop instead, but the migration prompt did not include CLAUDE.md edits in its step list so I did not touch it. Second, scripts/session-start-grounding.mjs (reads CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md from origin/main + injects as additionalContext) and scripts/session-stop-gate.mjs (blocks Stop when commits are ahead of origin/main) are still wired in settings.json alongside the new bash hooks; both implement the old doctrine and may want retirement once the comms v2 loop is confirmed working end-to-end across sessions. Third, CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md still lives at the repo root carrying the prior session's letter; the operator's deletion list did not include it so I left it in place, but under comms v2 it is structurally superseded by .carpenter/session.json and is a candidate for removal in a follow-up cut. None of these block the migration — the new loop is operational as soon as this session's session-close hook fires.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Operator to confirm the session-close hook actually fires on Stop in this environment; some environments are finicky about hook event firing. The hook was manually invoked at the end of the migration session to verify it writes a non-empty archive file and pushes cleanly. Also worth verifying that the next SessionStart pulls main and surfaces this file via the jq path in session-start.sh — that confirms the round-trip works end-to-end.
narrative.bigger_picture: Part of the AppCommander-wide doctrine shift consolidating five comms files to one and reducing each spawn's runtime dependency on AppCommander. The five-file bundle was structurally heavy for what it represented (point-in-time session state + flushed event log + dual-audience narratives + operational handoff), and the deferred-flush rule meant every session ended by writing five artifacts in one batch. The new shape is honest about what the artifact is — a single JSON file that the next session reads, the current session overwrites, the close hook archives + commits + pushes. Same loop, fewer files, no per-event append discipline to maintain. See AppCommander's COMMS_V2_AND_ADMIN_PAGE_SHIFT.md for full context.
